newsitem.title: UK: Marston to open 50 Pitcher & Piano by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Marston to open 50 Pitcher & Piano by 2000.

text.p: Brewer and pub owner Marston, Thompson & Evershed Plc plans to expand its chain of "Pitcher and Piano" bars to 50 from 10 by the year 2000, chairman Michael Hurdle said in an interview on Tuesday.
Pitcher and Piano achieved average sales per outlet of 20,600 stg per week and for the nine months of ownership contributed 1.4 million stg in profits before central costs of 0.5 million.

Analysts said the future growth of the company depends on its skills as a retailer and a test of this will be its ability to roll out more Pitcher and Piano bars. Brewing now accounts for only 10 percent of group profits.
The company added three Pitcher and Piano bars in the year to March 29, 1997 and plans to add nine more in the current financial year, said Hurdle.
"It's not just about site numbers but the size of the sites we are adding," said Hurdle.
The investment community criticised Marston in June 1996, for paying as much as 20 million stg for seven inner London Pitcher and Piano bars.

Earlier, Marston reported an 8.2 percent rise in its pre-tax profits to 29.5 million stg in the year to March 29, 1997. The group owns 245 managed pubs and 625 tenanted houses. Its retail division profits grew 17.5 percent to 18.4 million in the year.
Hurdle said there is currently a "feelgood factor" among consumers, which has contributed to an encouraging start to the current financial year.
"There is a delay in the budget starting to bite. The pain is yet to come. I think the customer on the high street hasn't had a bucket of cold water," said Hurdle.
Chancellor Gordon Brown announced his budget on July 2, which many economists think failed to quell consumer spending, leaving the central bank to tighten fiscal policy.

Marston shares bucked the general trend in the brewing sector on Tuesday to rise 7p to 276p near the close. Scottish and Newcastle Plc shares were down 3p at 690 while Whitbread Plc fell 14p to 785. Shares in Bass Plc were off 3p at 768.
